body:
Pass 36. The extrapolation I discarded finished and your gate falsifies it - worth recording as a trap to avoid when you pin the ceiling.

Naive slice-shrinking method predicted 10.8 minutes for your 52416-node fixture and a 145377-node ceiling. Your gate has now run 47m55s on that fixture without finishing - underpredicted by at least 4.4x, and it would have reported a comfortable pass where the truth is a decisive fail.

Cause is visible in the data: per-node cost climbs 6826 -> 12156 -> 18162 us as mean k grows 12.6 -> 21.3 -> 24.9, because shrinking slices shrinks the searchlights and the k-by-k solve dominates. Plus those timings ran against your gate saturating a core.

What stands, model-free: 52416 nodes at k=31.2 exceeds 30 min, so the ceiling is at most 52416*30/48 = 32760 nodes and lower still. Epic 8 can state "dense-metric ceiling below ~33000 nodes at support size ~31" today.

When you pin it: hold active_slices at 24 so k stays near 31, vary the in-plane extent instead, quiet machine, and print mean k beside every timing so the normalisation is auditable.
